newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-INDIA DROPPED FROM ALFRED DUNHILL CUP.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-INDIA DROPPED FROM ALFRED DUNHILL CUP.

text.p: India, who produced one of the shocks of the 1996 Alfred Dunhill Cup at St Andrews by beating Scotland, have been dropped from this year's event.
The unheralded Indian trio of Ali Sher, Gaurav Ghei and Jeev Singh were complete outsiders when they made their debut last year.
After losing narrowly to Zimbabwe in their first match, they upset Scotland 2-1 to leave themselves with a chance of reaching the semifinals.
But they lost 3-0 to Sweden on the third day to go out of the competition.
Former champions Canada along with Italy and Wales are the other countries from last year who have been dropped.
The four teams taking their places are Argentina, France, South Korea and Taiwan, who have all played in the tournament before.

The full list of competing countries for the Cup, which will be held at St Andrews from October 16-19, is: Argentina, Australia, England, France, Germany, Ireland, Japan, New Zealand, Scotland, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Taiwan, United States, Zimbabwe.
